question_stem:
The analogue signal from a microphone is to be transmitted in digital form.
The variation with time $t$ of part of the signal from the microphone is shown in Fig. 5.1.

{{figure:9702_w17_42_q05_figure_5_1}}

Fig. 5.1

The microphone output is sampled at a frequency of $5.0\text{kHz}$ by an analogue-to-digital converter (ADC).
The output from the ADC is a series of 4-bit numbers. The smallest bit represents $1.0\text{mV}$.
The first sample is taken at time $t = 0$.

parts.label: (a)
(b)
parts.text:
After transmission of the digital signal, it is converted back to an analogue signal using a digital-to-analogue converter (DAC).
Using data from Fig. 5.1, draw, on the axes of Fig. 5.3, the output level from the DAC for the transmitted signal from time $t = 0$ to time $t = 1.2\text{ms}$.

{{figure:9702_w17_42_q05_figure_5_3}}

Fig. 5.3

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
It is usual in modern telecommunication systems for the ADC and the DAC to have more than four bits in each sample.
State and explain the effect on the transmitted analogue signal of such an increase.
